chunks: And my father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to me from Sa'd ibn Abdillah, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Hamid al-Attar, from Abu Jamilah al-Mufaddal ibn Salih, from Abu Usamah Zayd al-Shahham, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Jibra'il (peace be upon him) announced the news of the killing of al-Husayn to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) in the house of Umm Salamah. Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) entered while Jibra'il was with him. Jibra'il said, 'Verily, your nation will kill him.' The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said, 'Show me from the dust upon which his blood will be shed.' So Jibra'il (peace be upon him) took a handful of that dust, and behold, it was red dust.

key_terms.أُمِّ سَلَمَةَ: Umm Salamah, a wife of the Prophet

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet Muhammad see when Jibra'il showed him the dust of Imam Husayn's martyrdom?
ai.summary: Recorded by Ibn Qulawayh in *Kamil al-Ziyarat*, this hadith emphasizes the divine foreknowledge of Imam al-Husayn’s martyrdom, linking the celestial announcement by Jibra’il to the earthly reality of Karbala. The presentation of red dust serves as a tangible sign (*ayat*) of the specific location and the sacrificial nature of his death, reinforcing the concept of *al-maqam al-mahmud* in Shia eschatology. This narrative underscores the continuity between prophetic revelation and the imamate, validating the Ahl al-Bayt’s authority through witnessed divine signs.

en.sayyid-mohsen-al-husayni-al-milani: 2. My father narrated to me from Sa’d ibn ‘Abdillāh, from Muḥammad ibn ‘Abdil Ḥamīd Al-‘Aťťār, from Abī Jamīlah Mufaďďal ibn Sāliḥ, from Abī Usāmah Zayd Al-Shaḥḥām, who said: Abū ‘Abdillāh (Imam Sādiq (a.s.)) said:

Jabra`īl announced the news of the killing of Ḥusain (a.s.) to the Messenger of Allāh (s.a.a.w.) in the house of Um Salamah. While Jabra`īl was with the Messenger of Allāh (s.a.a.w.), Ḥusain (a.s.) entered. Jabra`īl said to the Prophet (s.a.a.w.), “Verily your nation will kill him.” The Messenger of Allāh (s.a.a.w.) said, “Show me the dust on which his blood will be shed.” Jabra`īl took a handful of that dust and it was a red-coloured dust.
